## Highlights
Fans on Automatic now actually speed up when your Mac gets hot. The menu bar also gets the four-blade fan you see in the app.
This update changes ChillMac's fan helper, so macOS will ask you to approve ChillMac again under Login Items & Extensions. Fan control waits until you do. Later releases go back to one click.
## Fixed
- **Fans stuck at minimum on Automatic.** If ChillMac's fan helper restarted while it had the fans unlocked, it lost track of that and never handed them back to macOS. The fans then sat near their lowest speed no matter how hot the Mac got, until the next sleep or restart. The helper now notices and returns the fans to macOS. Smart and Manual cooling were not affected. - **"Fans are quiet" when they were not.** The header only looked at temperature, so it said the fans were quiet even with Smart on Cool spinning them at 4,000 RPM. It now checks the fans themselves. - **Diagnostics accuracy.** Exports no longer log idle fans held by macOS as manual, record battery temperature on macOS 27 instead of 0°, and skip the empty sample taken at launch.
## Changed
- **Menu bar icon.** Now the same four-blade fan used throughout the app.

Smart cooling now takes over the fans on its own after ChillMac starts.
## Fixed
- **Fans waited for the menu bar to be opened.** At login or right after an update, ChillMac's fan helper can take a few seconds to start, and ChillMac only checked on it again when you opened the menu bar. Until then the fans stayed with macOS. ChillMac now keeps checking in the background and takes over as soon as the helper is ready.
Temperatures, the menu bar reading and the detail panels were accurate throughout. Only the start of Smart cooling was delayed.

Battery details are back on macOS 27.
## Fixed
- **Battery capacity.** On macOS 27, Current and Original capacity both showed 100 mAh, because macOS moved where it reports them. ChillMac now finds the real figures, and says "Not reported" if a Mac doesn't provide one. - **Battery temperature.** macOS 27 stopped reporting it in the usual place, so the Battery panel showed 0°. ChillMac now reads it from the Mac's own battery sensors instead.
Only the Battery panel was affected. Fan control, the menu bar reading and the other panels were accurate throughout.
